messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: wouldn't get complete labeling of the tips
parts:
Ah, I see.  That's just an issue with the APE plot function.  There actually is an option I put into plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() at some point to deal with this. It is "xlims:


xlims 
# Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
#' if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight)

So, if your tree is 83 million years old at the root, add this option to the plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() command:

xlims=c(0,1.5*83)

Adjust "1.5" as needed, until it looks right. 



Additional helpful options of plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() -- make sure to do 
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")

...to enable.

=====================
* tiplabel_adj Justification for tiplabel boxes (same as "adj" parameter of text() ). Default is c(0.5). Left justification: c(0). Right: c(1). Justification top left: c(0,0), etc.

* You can also change "tipcex" (tip character expansion)
tipcex cex value for the tiplabels (scaling factor, i.e. 0.5 is half size)

* show.tip.label Same as for APE's \code{plot.phylo}.

* xlims Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight).

* ylims Same as in plot.phylo y.lim. Default is basically c(0,numtips), so
if the spacing between the title and time axis and the tree are too big,
try e.g. ylims=c(0+10,numtips-10). Trial and error will get you there. 

See: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-phylo/2013-March/002540.html
=====================

Another option is show.tip.label=FALSE, then use the text() command to plot tip labels yourself.  Yet another option is manual editing/fixing of the tip labels etc. in Adobe Illustrator or in Inkscape (which is similar but free).

Cheers,
Nick

Hi -- "pasting problem"?  Not sure what that means.

If what you meant is, your tip labels are being cut off, try:

On Monday, October 16, 2017 at 8:45:08 AM UTC+5, Nick Matzke wrote:
Ah, I see.  That's just an issue with the APE plot function.  There actually is an option I put into plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() at some point to deal with this. It is "xlims:


xlims 
# Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
#' if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight)

So, if your tree is 83 million years old at the root, add this option to the plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() command:

xlims=c(0,1.5*83)

Adjust "1.5" as needed, until it looks right. 



Additional helpful options of plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() -- make sure to do 
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")

...to enable.

=====================
* tiplabel_adj Justification for tiplabel boxes (same as "adj" parameter of text() ). Default is c(0.5). Left justification: c(0). Right: c(1). Justification top left: c(0,0), etc.

* You can also change "tipcex" (tip character expansion)
tipcex cex value for the tiplabels (scaling factor, i.e. 0.5 is half size)

* show.tip.label Same as for APE's \code{plot.phylo}.

* xlims Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight).

* ylims Same as in plot.phylo y.lim. Default is basically c(0,numtips), so
if the spacing between the title and time axis and the tree are too big,
try e.g. ylims=c(0+10,numtips-10). Trial and error will get you there. 

See: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-phylo/2013-March/002540.html
=====================

Another option is show.tip.label=FALSE, then use the text() command to plot tip labels yourself.  Yet another option is manual editing/fixing of the tip labels etc. in Adobe Illustrator or in Inkscape (which is similar but free).

Cheers,
Nick
